entries.action: HARDEN the R-BODY-1 uniform-pool control into a rule: no learned pooling before P1 passes on a variant. Any future learned-pooling proposal must beat uniform in-probe on the P1 stacking metric, not on train fit. Also confirms C1 (learned≡uniform) was the right call to keep as control.
entries.note: Chronos-2 group-attention decomposition via inference-time attention-matrix editing: uniform pooling (V/O projection of an unweighted summary, no Q/K weighting) is positive on 18/20 sensor-network configs, while the learned Q/K weighting is positive/negligible for multivariate but materially degrades 8/10 in-context-learning configs (4 worse than univariate inference). Uniforming alpha in the first block alone improves every ICL config tested.
entries.relevance: R-BODY-1 pooling rule (uniform control locked) + C1 confirmation.
entries.title: Pooling Helps, Learned Weighting Hurts In-Context: Decomposing Group Attention

entries.action: No design change: converges with the MAP v5 WRONG-CLASS verdict and the CYCLE-217 linear-first doctrine from the finance side. Cite when the doctrine is next challenged: SOTA time-series transformers underperform even vanilla transformers on financial tasks.
entries.note: SOTA time-series transformers often underperform even vanilla transformers on financial tasks (stationarity assumptions violated by regime shifts); simpler CNN/RNN architectures with distinct inductive biases achieve stronger performance at lower complexity; no single inductive bias dominates across markets or regimes. TIPS distills bias-specialized teachers (causality, locality, periodicity via attention masking) with regime-dependent alignment: +55%/+9%/+16% annual return/Sharpe/Calmar over strong ensembles at 38% inference compute.
entries.title: Integrating Inductive Biases in Transformers via Distillation for Financial Time Series Forecasting

entries.action: P5 protocol amendment (behind P1): a TTA/fitness comparison must name and validate its deployment policy (rollout/selection rule), not just its architecture — the policy is a free, low-cost adaptiveness source. Metric-sensitivity warning: an MSE-selected policy does not transfer uniformly to finance losses (QLIKE) — our skill-vs-base convention is the named metric, keep it.
entries.note: A trained multi-output forecaster does not define a single deployable predictor: changing the inference-time rollout rule induces a family of forecasts with different accuracy/cost profiles (20 stock-vol series, 3 horizons, linear to PatchTST). Non-default rules often beat standard MIMO deployment, but the best fixed rule varies by architecture/horizon; validation-selected singletons give low-cost improvement, small subsets recover much of ensemble benefit at lower cost. Policy rankings are metric-sensitive (MSE-selected policies do not transfer uniformly to QLIKE).
entries.relevance: P5/R-TTA protocol: validate the deployment policy; metric-sensitivity caution.
entries.title: Deployment-Side Adaptiveness in Multi-Horizon Volatility Forecasting

entries.action: Dormant TODO 97 trigger design (no live work): when a re-train cadence question re-opens, the trigger candidate is realized-forecast-error dynamics (pseudo-label from future error increases, lightweight scorer, plug-in, backbone-agnostic — validated on DLinear/iTransformer/TimesNet), NOT drift alarms or staleness. entries.note: PILOT: online retraining framework that learns WHEN to retrain from forecast-error dynamics. Pseudo-label from future increases in forecast error trains a lightweight scorer on observed error states; deployment uses only completed forecast errors, plug-in for arbitrary backbones. SOTA average-rank among retraining policies across 8 benchmarks x DLinear/iTransformer/TimesNet with favorable performance-efficiency trade-off.
entries.title: Pseudo-Label-Triggered Retraining from Forecast Errors for Online Time Series Forecasting

entries.action: Methodology caution for the Brier path and all pooled readouts (C6 top-K, legion pooling, selection protocols): audit regime-wise bias, never aggregate-only. A loss's estimand sets an intrinsic bias floor no training can remove; pooled training allocates systematic mismatch across pathological subpopulations invisibly to aggregate metrics. Applies if/when a P1 family passes and selection work resumes.
entries.note: Canonical losses embed fixed statistical priors; industrial demand mixes benign and pathological regimes where priors are violated; induced bias persists under perfect temporal modeling, sits in a distributional-shape component normalization cannot remove, creates an aggregation trade-off invisible to aggregate metrics. RBV (regime-wise relative bias vector) diagnostic + attribution into model-independent intrinsic floor (loss's estimand) vs train-attributable excess. 13 losses, 3 seeds, 60k+ series: regime-aware diagnosis separates optimization- from bias-type failure; regime-aware training resolves pooling-induced bias capacity scaling cannot. Risk under evaluation-distribution contamination is affine in pathology mixture weight.
entries.relevance: Loss/pooling methodology caution (Brier path, C6, selection).
entries.title: Beyond Model Ranking: Regime Diagnosis for Distributional-Statistical Misspecification

entries.action: Channel-design contrast for R-BODY-1/2 (behind P1): SSM-shaped alternative to the xCPD spectral-routing rule — data-dependent fine-grained cross-variable interaction at linear cost, CI vs CD framing. No design change: both rules wait behind P1; a future channel-interaction proposal picks one and beats the other in-probe.
entries.note: Chameleon: channel-dependent SSM with data-dependent fine-grained cross-variable interaction scaling linearly with variable count (selective SSM + Kalman missing-measurement update for cross-variable modeling, GatedDeltaNet backbone, stochastic RevIN perturbation). On strongly-dependent sets beats CI ablation and prior CD methods by 61-178% higher-MSE margin; best MSE/MAE in 27+/22 of 28 standard settings.
entries.title: Channel-Dependent State Space Model for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
